akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّسْرِفِينَ﴾: He means "because you were".

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ﴾: making it masculine is allowed with reference to ﴿مَا تَرْكَبُونَ﴾, and ﴿ما﴾ is masculine, as you say: "عندي من النساء ما يوافقك ويسرك" (I have, of women, what will suit you and please you, with masculine verbs). "الانعام" (cattle) may be masculine or feminine: in one place He said ﴿مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ and in another place He said ﴿بُطُونِها﴾.

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾: the Arabs say "أَنَا بَراءٌ منك" (I am free of you).

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ﴾: its like is the Arabs' saying "مَفاتِح" and "مَفَاتِيح" (keys), "مَعَاطٍ" from "المِعطاءِ" (the generous giver), and "أَثَافٍ" from "الأُثِفِيَّةِ" (hearth-stone). The singular of "المعَارِج" is "المِعْراج" (stairway); if you wish you say in its plural "المعارِيج".

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿وَإِن كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: light, with the lām with fatḥa. Some read ﴿لمّا﴾, making it heavy, with fatḥa on the lām and the mīm doubled, and claimed that it, in the first interpretation, (means) "إلاّ" (except), and that it is from the speech of the Arabs.

akhfash:36-36.t:
And He said ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾: it is not from "أَعْشى" (night-blind) and "عَشْو"; it has only the meaning of the poet's words [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 267]:
* إلَى مالِكٍ أَعْشو الى مِثْلِ مالِكِ *
(To Mālik I turn with weak sight — to the like of Mālik.)
As though "أَعْشُو" meant "I am weak". For when he said "I turn with weak sight to the like of Mālik", "العَشْوُ" was weakness, because when he said "I turn with weak sight to the like of Mālik" he informed that he comes to him neither seeing nor strong. As he said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 268]:
مَتَى تَأْتِهِ تَعْشُو إِلَى ضَوْءِ نارِهِ * تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وَنَاراً تَأَجَّجَا
(Whenever you come to him, making your way dimly to the light of his fire, you will find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)
i.e. whenever you become poor and make for the light of his fire, he will enrich you.

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ﴾ because "أساور" and "أسْوِرَة" are plurals (of سِوار, bracelet). Some read ﴿أَساورة﴾, making it a plural of "الأسورة"; he meant "أَسَاوِير" — and Allah knows best — and made the hāʾ a compensation for the yāʾ, just as one said "زَنَادِقَة", making the hāʾ a compensation for the yāʾ in "زَنَادِيق" (heretics).

akhfash:57-57.t: And He said ﴿يَصُدُّونَ﴾ and ﴿يَصِدُّون﴾, just as He said ﴿يَحْشُرُ﴾ and ﴿يَحْشِرُ﴾.

daas-irab:1-8.t: ﴿حم وَالْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ﴾ the i'rab of the like of it has already been given; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿جَعَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿قُرْآناً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عَرَبِيًّا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of قرآنا, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position; ﴿قُرْآناً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عَرَبِيًّا﴾ an adjective of قرآنا, and the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position «[Translator's note: these last two items are repeated in the source.]»; ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun; ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position; ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; ﴿فِي أُمِّ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to علي; ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿لَدَيْنا﴾ an adverb of place, a badal (substitute) for في أم; ﴿لَعَلِيٌّ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and علي is the first khabar of inna; ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ a second khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation expressing disapproval and rebuke, and the fāʾ is a conjunction to something omitted, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿عَنْكُمُ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الذِّكْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿صَفْحاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar particle; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its khabar; ﴿مُسْرِفِينَ﴾ an adjective of قوما, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by a preposition, and both are attached to نضرب; ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and كم is predicative (khabariyya), in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of أرسلنا; ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿نَبِيٍّ﴾ the tamyīz (specification) of كم; ﴿فِي الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative; ﴿يَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant preposition; ﴿نَبِيٍّ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb after them; ﴿يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) excepted from the generality of states; ﴿فَأَهْلَكْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿أَشَدَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to أشد; ﴿بَطْشاً﴾ tamyīz; ﴿وَمَضى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, and the clause is conjoined to أهلكنا; ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:9-12.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām paves the way for (muwaṭṭiʾa) an omitted oath, and إن is conditional; ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the voweled tāʾ of the agent, and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السموات, and the clause من خلق is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the second mafʿūl bihi of سألتهم, and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of من; ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the nūn having been dropped because of the dislike of a succession of identical letters, and the dropped wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis (tawkīd), and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْعَزِيزُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for العزيز, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a badal for العليم; ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مَهْداً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and وجعل لكم is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿سُبُلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun; ﴿تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of لعلكم, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿وَالَّذِي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the relative noun is conjoined to the first relative; ﴿نَزَّلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿ماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بِقَدَرٍ﴾ both attached to the verb as well; ﴿فَأَنْشَرْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿بَلْدَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مَيْتاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿تُخْرَجُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the verbal clause is resumptive; ﴿وَالَّذِي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and الذي is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿الْأَزْواجَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كُلَّها﴾ tawkīd (emphasis); ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مِنَ الْفُلْكِ﴾ both attached to تركبون; ﴿وَالْأَنْعامِ﴾ conjoined to الفلك; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿تَرْكَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:13-16.t: ﴿لِتَسْتَوُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and both are attached (mutaʿalliq) to جعل; ﴿عَلى ظُهُورِهِ﴾ both attached to تستووا; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿تَذْكُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿نِعْمَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رَبِّكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿إِذَا﴾ an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿اسْتَوَيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَتَقُولُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and the wāw is fāʿil; ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿سَخَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿هذا﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ما is negative; ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to مقرنين; ﴿مُقْرِنِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of كنا, and the clause ما كنا is circumstantial; ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and inna and its noun; ﴿إِلى رَبِّنا﴾ both attached to منقلبون; ﴿لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and منقلبون is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿وَجَعَلُوا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to the verb, and they stand as the second object; ﴿مِنْ عِبادِهِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿جُزْءاً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَكَفُورٌ﴾ the shifted lām, and كفور is the khabar of inna; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of كفور, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿أَمِ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of بل (rather); ﴿اتَّخَذَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿يَخْلُقُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بَناتٍ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi, and the preposition and its genitive noun before it stand as the second object; ﴿وَأَصْفاكُمْ﴾ conjoined to اتخذ; ﴿بِالْبَنِينَ﴾ both attached to the verb.

daas-irab:17-21.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and إذا is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿بُشِّرَ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿أَحَدُهُمْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿بِما﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿ضَرَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; ﴿لِلرَّحْمنِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the first being omitted; ﴿ظَلَّ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿وَجْهُهُ﴾ its noun; ﴿مُسْوَدًّا﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿أَوَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation expressing disapproval, and the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb; ﴿يُنَشَّؤُا﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; ﴿فِي الْحِلْيَةِ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative; ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿فِي الْخِصامِ﴾ both attached to مبين; ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿وَجَعَلُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿الْمَلائِكَةَ﴾ its first mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of الملائكة; ﴿هُمْ عِبادُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿إِناثاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿أَشَهِدُوا﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation expressing rebuke, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿خَلْقَهُمْ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿سَتُكْتَبُ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and a passive imperfect verb; ﴿شَهادَتُهُمْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَيُسْئَلُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿عَبَدْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar; ﴿بِذلِكَ﴾ both attached to علم; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿يَخْرُصُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿آتَيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كِتاباً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of كتابا, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to مستمسكون; ﴿مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:22-26.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb); ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿وَجَدْنا آباءَنا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿عَلى أُمَّةٍ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; ﴿عَلى آثارِهِمْ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ the khabar of inna, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿فِي قَرْيَةٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿نَذِيرٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿مُتْرَفُوها﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, the nūn having been dropped because of the annexation, and the clause is circumstantial, excepted from the generality of states; ﴿إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُقْتَدُونَ﴾ its i'rab has already been given; ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿أَوَلَوْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and لو is conditional; ﴿جِئْتُكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿بِأَهْدى﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to أهدى; ﴿وَجَدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿آباءَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause أولو is the object of the saying; ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to كافرون; ﴿أُرْسِلْتُمْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying; ﴿فَانْتَقَمْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿فَانْظُرْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted khabar; ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿عاقِبَةُ﴾ its noun; ﴿الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the clause فانظر is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position, and the clause كيف كان stands in place of the object of انظر; ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an adverb of time; ﴿قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿لِأَبِيهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَقَوْمِهِ﴾ conjoined to أبيه; ﴿إِنَّنِي بَراءٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the nominal clause is the object of the saying; ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to براء; ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:27-31.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ excepted by إلا; ﴿فَطَرَنِي﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and inna and its noun; ﴿سَيَهْدِينِ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ, dropped to suit the verse-ending (fāṣila), is mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿وَجَعَلَها﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; ﴿كَلِمَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿باقِيَةً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِي عَقِبِهِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to باقية; ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun; ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿مَتَّعْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَآباءَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; ﴿جاءَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ a postponed fāʿil, and the implied أن and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb; ﴿وَرَسُولٌ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective of رسول; ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لما is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿جاءَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ a postponed fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿هذا سِحْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna and its noun; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to كافرون; ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ the khabar of inna, nominative by the wāw, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); ﴿نُزِّلَ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿هذَا﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿الْقُرْآنُ﴾ badal (substitute); ﴿عَلى رَجُلٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of رجل; ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾ a second adjective, and the clause لولا نزل is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:32-34.t: ﴿أَهُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَقْسِمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); ﴿رَحْمَتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿قَسَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar; ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ مَعِيشَتَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِي الْحَياةِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of الحياة, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿وَرَفَعْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بَعْضَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿بَعْضٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿دَرَجاتٍ﴾ tamyīz (specification); ﴿لِيَتَّخِذَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb; ﴿بَعْضَهُمْ﴾ fāʿil «[Translator's note: so in the source, although the word is vocalised in the accusative here; in the verse it is بَعْضُهُمْ.]»; ﴿بَعْضاً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿سُخْرِيًّا﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَرَحْمَتُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to خير; ﴿يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لولا is a conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the accusative by أن, and الناس is its noun; ﴿أُمَّةً﴾ its khabar; ﴿واحِدَةً﴾ an adjective, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted, and the clause لولا is resumptive; ﴿لَجَعَلْنا﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the preposition and its genitive noun stand as the second object; ﴿يَكْفُرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بِالرَّحْمنِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿لِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for لمن; ﴿سُقُفاً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of سقفا; ﴿وَمَعارِجَ﴾ conjoined to سقفا; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ both attached to يظهرون; ﴿يَظْهَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of معارج; ﴿وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both conjoined to what precedes them; ﴿أَبْواباً﴾ conjoined to سقفا; ﴿وَسُرُراً﴾ conjoined to what preceded; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿يَتَّكِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of سررا.

daas-irab:35-38.t: ﴿وَزُخْرُفاً﴾ conjoined to سررا; ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and إن is negative; ﴿كُلُّ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿لَمَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) in the sense of إلا; ﴿مَتاعُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿الْحَياةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿وَالْآخِرَةُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَعْشُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿نُقَيِّضْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿شَيْطاناً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to قرين; ﴿قَرِينٌ﴾ khabar, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and inna and its noun; ﴿لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl; ﴿عَنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun «[Translator's note: so in the source: the word is written إِنَّهُمْ but parsed as أنّ; the verse has أَنَّهُمْ.]»; ﴿مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ its khabar, and أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of يحسبون; ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿جاءَنا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position; ﴿يا﴾ a particle of alerting (tanbīh); ﴿لَيْتَ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿بَيْنِي﴾ an adverb attached to the omitted fronted khabar of layta; ﴿وَبَيْنَكَ﴾ conjoined to بيني; ﴿بُعْدَ﴾ the postponed noun of layta; ﴿الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the nominal clause يا ليت is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿فَبِئْسَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and a past verb for expressing blame; ﴿الْقَرِينُ﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:39-43.t: ﴿وَلَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لن is a particle making the verb accusative; ﴿يَنْفَعَكُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb), and the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time, a badal (substitute) for اليوم; ﴿ظَلَمْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the clause لن ينفعكم is resumptive; ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾ anna and its noun; ﴿فِي الْعَذابِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to what follows them; ﴿مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of ينفعكم; ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the fāʾ is resumptive, and أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar of أنت, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a conjunction, and من is conjoined to العمي; ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent; ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ its khabar; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ضلال; ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and إما is a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; ﴿نَذْهَبَنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and it is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿بِكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿فَإِنَّا﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and inna and its noun; ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾ its khabar, nominative by the wāw, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿نُرِيَنَّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb conjoined to نذهبن; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَعَدْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُقْتَدِرُونَ﴾ like the i'rab of the previous verse; ﴿فَاسْتَمْسِكْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿بِالَّذِي﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is the apodosis of a condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿أُوحِيَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿عَلى صِراطٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar; ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:44-47.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; ﴿لَذِكْرٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ذكر is khabar (predicate); ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to ذكر, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾ conjoined to لك; ﴿وَسَوْفَ﴾ a resumptive particle and a particle of the future; ﴿تُسْئَلُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَسْئَلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause اسأل is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مِنْ رُسُلِنا﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿أَجَعَلْنا﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation expressing disapproval, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the second mafʿūl bihi of اسأل; ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ both attached to يعبدون; ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يُعْبَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of آلهة; ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ both attached to the verb as well; ﴿وَمَلَائِهِ﴾ conjoined to فرعون; ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿إِنِّي رَسُولُ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قال is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿رَبِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ; ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ a resumptive particle, and لما is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿إِذا﴾ of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مِنْها﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿يَضْحَكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) has no grammatical position because it is the response to لما.

daas-irab:48-51.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿نُرِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida); ﴿آيَةٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿هِيَ أَكْبَرُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿مِنْ أُخْتِها﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to أكبر; ﴿وَأَخَذْناهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿بِالْعَذابِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun; ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of لعلهم, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā); ﴿السَّاحِرُ﴾ an adjective of أيها; ﴿ادْعُ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿رَبَّكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to ادع; ﴿عَهِدَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿عِنْدَكَ﴾ an adverb of place, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿إِنَّنا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَمُهْتَدُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and مهتدون is its khabar, nominative by the wāw, and what comes after the verb of saying is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and لما is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿كَشَفْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿عَنْهُمُ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِذا﴾ of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَنْكُثُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿وَنادى﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb; ﴿فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فِي قَوْمِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause قال is explicative (tafsīriyya); ﴿يا قَوْمِ﴾ the one addressed, annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which has been dropped, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying; ﴿أَلَيْسَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its fronted khabar; ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ its postponed noun; ﴿مِصْرَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa because it is a diptote; ﴿وَهذِهِ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ badal (substitute); ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the fāʾ is resumptive, and لا is negative; ﴿تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:52-57.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ هذَا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to خير; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿مَهِينٌ﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negative; ﴿يَكادُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿يُبِينُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, and the clause is the khabar of يكاد, and the clause لا يكاد is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); ﴿أُلْقِيَ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿أَسْوِرَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْ ذَهَبٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of أسورة; ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿جاءَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿مُقْتَرِنِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَاسْتَخَفَّ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿قَوْمَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿فَأَطاعُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its khabar, and the clause كانوا is the khabar of إنهم, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿فاسِقِينَ﴾ an adjective of قوما; ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and لما is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿آسَفُونا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿انْتَقَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis), accusative by the yāʾ; ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿سَلَفاً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَمَثَلًا﴾ conjoined to سلفا; ﴿لِلْآخِرِينَ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of مثلا; ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لما is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿ضُرِبَ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿ابْنُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿إِذا﴾ of surprise (fujāʾiyya); ﴿قَوْمُكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿يَصِدُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. «[Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere the book treats the clause after إذا of surprise as the apodosis of لما, with no grammatical position.]»

daas-irab:58-62.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿آلِهَتُنا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿هُوَ﴾ conjoined to آلهتنا; ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿ضَرَبُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿جَدَلًا﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿بَلْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿هُمْ قَوْمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿خَصِمُونَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of قوم, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; ﴿عَبْدٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَنْعَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of عبد; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَجَعَلْناهُ﴾ conjoined to أنعمنا; ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of جعلناه; ﴿لِبَنِي﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of مثلا; ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لو is a conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿لَجَعَلْنا﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb, and they stand in the place of the first object; ﴿مَلائِكَةً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿يَخْلُفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of ملائكة; ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; ﴿لَعِلْمٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and علم is the khabar of inna; ﴿لِلسَّاعَةِ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of علم, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and لا is prohibitive; ﴿تَمْتَرُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; ﴿بِها﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَاتَّبِعُونِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the first-person yāʾ, dropped for lightening, is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿صِراطٌ﴾ khabar; ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), and the clause اتبعون is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is prohibitive; ﴿يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive by the prohibitive لا, and the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to عدو; ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾ the khabar of inna; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective of عدو, and the nominal clause is causal, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:63-66.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لما is an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿جاءَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿عِيسى﴾ fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿جِئْتُكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَلِأُبَيِّنَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to what precedes them; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿بَعْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَاتَّقُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ conjoined to فاتقوا; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Divine Name is its noun; ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿رَبِّي﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الله is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَرَبُّكُمْ﴾ conjoined to ربي; ﴿فَاعْبُدُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿هذا صِراطٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and a past verb; ﴿الْأَحْزابُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ both attached to an omitted second khabar; ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ an adjective of عذاب; ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle; ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿السَّاعَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by أن, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is a badal (substitute) for الساعة; ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ ḥāl; ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is circumstantial.

daas-irab:67-72.t: ﴿الْأَخِلَّاءُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time, and إذ is an adverb for past time; ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to عدو; ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of بعضهم, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ excepted by إلا, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, and the nominal clause الأخلاء is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿يا عِبادِ﴾ يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the dropped first-person yāʾ, and the first-person yāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿خَوْفٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negative; ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿تَحْزَنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for عبادي; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and kāna and its noun; ﴿مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿ادْخُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; ﴿الْجَنَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of the omitted saying; ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿وَأَزْواجُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to the mubtadaʾ; ﴿تُحْبَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُطافُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb, and they stand in the place of the nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿بِصِحافٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مِنْ ذَهَبٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of صحاف; ﴿وَأَكْوابٍ﴾ conjoined to صحاف; ﴿وَفِيها﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar; ﴿ما﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿تَشْتَهِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْأَنْفُسُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَتَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾ khabar, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَتِلْكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْجَنَّةُ﴾ khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of الجنة; ﴿أُورِثْتُمُوها﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil, and the wāw results from vowel-lengthening (ishbāʿ), and ها is its second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of kāna.

daas-irab:73-80.t: ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to the same khabar; ﴿فاكِهَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿كَثِيرَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿مِنْها﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is an adjective of فاكهة; ﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿فِي عَذابِ﴾ both attached to the khabar; ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾ the khabar of inna, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يُفَتَّرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿مُبْلِسُونَ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿ظَلَمْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk); ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the khabar of كانوا, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَنادَوْا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿يا مالِكُ﴾ يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative, and the vocative clause is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi; ﴿لِيَقْضِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿إِنَّكُمْ ماكِثُونَ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿جِئْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and لكن is a particle resembling the verb; ﴿أَكْثَرَكُمْ﴾ its noun; ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿كارِهُونَ﴾ the khabar of lākinna, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿أَمْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿أَبْرَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَمْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فَإِنَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; ﴿مُبْرِمُونَ﴾ its khabar, nominative by the wāw, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَمْ﴾ a particle of digression in the sense of بل (rather); ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿نَسْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿سِرَّهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the khabar of anna; ﴿وَنَجْواهُمْ﴾ conjoined to سرهم, and أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of يحسبون; ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; ﴿وَرُسُلُنا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿يَكْتُبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:81-85.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional; ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿لِلرَّحْمنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿وَلَدٌ﴾ the postponed noun of kāna, and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَأَنَا﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَوَّلُ﴾ its khabar; ﴿الْعابِدِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis; ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; ﴿رَبِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi as well; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ﴾ a badal (substitute) for رب السموات; ﴿عَمَّا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the mafʿūl muṭlaq; ﴿يَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَذَرْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿يَخُوضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the response to the command (jawāb al-ṭalab), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; ﴿وَيَلْعَبُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; ﴿يُلاقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يخوضوا; ﴿يَوْمَهُمُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of يومهم; ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar; ﴿إِلهٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلهٌ﴾ conjoined; ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and هو is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ two khabars, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَتَبارَكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات, and the nominal clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿وَعِنْدَهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and عنده is an adverb of place attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿عِلْمُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿السَّاعَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إليه are both attached to what follows them; ﴿تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:86-89.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لا is negative; ﴿يَمْلِكُ﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to يدعون; ﴿الشَّفاعَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿مِنْ﴾ excepted by إلا «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the word is the relative مَنْ.]»; ﴿شَهِدَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the lām paves the way for (muwaṭṭiʾa) the omitted oath; ﴿إن﴾ conditional; ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and it is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿خَلَقَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause stands in place of the second object of سألتهم; ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is fāʿil, and the final nūn is the nūn of emphasis (tawkīd); ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ليقولن is the response to an implied oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl; ﴿يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَقِيلِهِ﴾ the wāw is a preposition and a particle of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb of oath; ﴿يا رَبِّ﴾ يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the dropped first-person yāʾ; ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of قوم; ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb «[Translator's note: the source passes over the word فَاصْفَحْ that precedes عنهم in the verse; it is evidently the verb meant here, and the next item refers to it as اصفح.]»; ﴿وَقُلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying, and the verbal clause is conjoined to اصفح; ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and سوف is a particle of deferral (taswīf) and of the future; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَن كُنتُمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: "إن كنتم" with kasra, and ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read: "أنْ كنتم" with fatḥa on (أنْ), as though they meant something past. In ordinary speech you say: "Shall I revile you أن you deprived me?", meaning "since (إذ) you deprived me"; and you use kasra when you mean: "Shall I revile you if (إن) you deprive me?" Like it is: ﴿ولاَ يَجْرِمَنّكُمْ شَنآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكم﴾: you may read (إن) with kasra or with fatḥa.
And like it: ﴿فلعلَّك باخعٌ نفسك على آثارِهم﴾ "إن لم يؤمنوا" and "أن لم يؤمنوا". The Arabs recite the saying of al-Farazdaq:
أتجزع إن أذنا قتيبة حزتا * جهاراً، ولم تجزع لقتل ابن خازم؟
(Do you grieve if [or: that] the two ears of Qutayba were cut off openly, yet you did not grieve at the killing of Ibn Khāzim?)
And they recited to me:
أتجزع أن بان الخليط المودّع * وجبل الصفا من عزة المتقطع؟
(Do you grieve that the departing companions have parted, and the bond of affection with ʿAzza that is cut?)
And in each of the two verses there is what is in its companion: kasra and fatḥa. And the Arabs say: "I have turned away (أضربت) from you" and "I turned (ضربت) from you", when they mean by it: I left you and I turned aside from you.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ﴾.
Someone may say: how did He say "على ظهوره" (on its backs), attaching "backs" to a singular? It is said to him: that singular is in the meaning of a plural, in the same way as "the troops", "the army" and "the whole body". If he says: then why did you not say "لتستووا على ظهره" (on its back), making "back" singular when you attach it to a singular? I say: the singular contains the meaning of the plural, so I returned "backs" to the meaning and did not say "its back", lest it be like the singular whose meaning and wording are both singular. Likewise you say: "The women of the troops (الجند) have become many", and you say: "The troops raised their eyes (أعينه)", and do not say "its eye (عينه)". And likewise everything you attach to such of the concrete nouns, you bring out in the plural; but when you attach to it a noun in the meaning of an action (fiʿl), both its plural and its singular are allowed, as in your saying: "The troops raised their voice (صوته)" and "their voices (أصواته)", which is better. This is allowed because the action has no form in the dual other than its form in the singular.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ﴾.
Capable of it (muṭīqīn). You say to a man: "You have become مُقرن for this", i.e. you are capable of it and have become a match (qirn) for it.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً﴾.
The verb belongs to the face, so for that reason you put the predicate (fiʿl) in the accusative; and had you made "ظلّ" belong to the man, you would put "the face" and "blackened" in the nominative, saying: ظل وجهه مسودٌّ وهو كظيم.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي ٱلْحِلْيَةِ﴾.
He means the females. He says: you have assigned daughters to the All-Merciful, while you are such that when a daughter is born to one of you, what He described befalls him. As for His saying ﴿أومَنْ﴾, it is as though He said: "and one who is not brought up except in ornaments, and who in dispute is not clear", i.e. does not attain in argument what a man attains. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أَوَمَنْ لا يُنَشَّأُ إلاّ فى الْحِلْيَةِ". If you wish [169/b], you put "مَن" in the position of the nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf); and if you wish, you put it in the accusative by an implied verb, "they make (يجعلون)" or the like; and if you refer it back to the beginning of the speech, to His saying: "وإِذَ بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِما ضَرَبَ", you put it in the genitive [and if you wish, in the accusative]. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, the companions of ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: "يُنَشَّأُ", and ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz read: ينْشَأُ فى الحلية.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿عِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlqama and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it: "عباد الرحمن"; and it is reported [of] ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him) that he read it: "عند الرحمن", and likewise ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz, as though they took that from His saying: ﴿إنَّ الذين عِنْد رَبِّك لا يَسْتَكْبِرُون عَنْ عِبادَتهِ﴾. All is correct.
His saying: ﴿أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash gave the alif of "أشهدوا" fatḥa, and the people of the Ḥijāz gave it ḍamma, in the interpretation: أُشْهدوا خلقهم ("were they made to witness their creation?"), because its agent is not named; and the meaning is the same. They read it without hamza, intending the question. Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: so al-Farrāʾ said.

farraa:22-23.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ آبَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
The readers read it with ḍamma on the alif of "أُمّة", and Mujāhid and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read it with kasra. It is as though al-imma is like sunna (custom) and milla (creed); and al-imma is the way (ṭarīqa), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "I led (amamtu) the people". The Arabs say: "How fine is his imma, his ʿimma and his jilsa!", when it is a maṣdar. Al-imma is also dominion and bliss. ʿAdī said:
ثم بعْدَ الفلاحِ والمُلكِ والإمّة * وارثهمُ هناك القبورُ
(Then, after prosperity, dominion and imma, the graves there have concealed them.)
As though he meant the leadership of dominion and its bliss.
«[Translator's note: «وارثهم» as printed is translated by its evident sense "concealed them" (cf. واراهم); the verse is cited elsewhere as «وارتهم».]»
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾ and ﴿مُّقْتَدُونَ﴾.
They are nominative; had they been accusative, that would have been allowed, because stopping before them is good. So you say to a man: "You came while we were following the track (متبعين / متبعون)".

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾.
The Arabs say: "We are barāʾ and khalāʾ of you" (quit of you); and for the singular, the dual and the plural, feminine and masculine, one says: barāʾ, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Had He said (برىء), one would say in the dual: بريئان, and of a group: بريئون and برءاء. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "إنَّنى بَرِئٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُون"; and had a reader read it so, it would be correct and in agreement with our reading [i.e. our codex], because the Arabs write يستهزىء as يستهزأ, writing the hamza with alif in all its states. They write شىء as شيأ, and the like is frequent in the codices of ʿAbd Allāh; and in our codex: ويهيىء لكم is written ويهيأ, with alif.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ﴾.
[It is] the name of Islam. He says: binding on whoever followed him and was of his offspring; perhaps the people of Mecca will follow this religion, since they are of the offspring of Abraham, Allah bless him. That is His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: to your religion and the religion of Abraham, Allah bless them both.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾.
Its meaning is: on one of two men; he meant himself and Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. It was al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī who said this. The two towns are Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ﴾.
So We raised the master above his slave, and made some of them take others captive, so the slave and the one taken captive are made subservient to those above them.
His saying: ﴿لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضاً سُخْرِيّاً﴾, and "سِخْرِيّاً": they are one here and in "قد أفلح" [al-Muʾminūn] and in Ṣād; kasra and ḍamma in them are the same, two dialects.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
أن is in the position of the nominative.
His saying: ﴿لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾.
If you wish, you make the lām repeated in لبيوتهم, as He said: ﴿يسَأَلُونكَ عن الشَّهرِ الْحَرامِ قِتَالٍ فيه﴾; and if you wish, you make the two lāms different, as though the second were in the meaning of على, as though He said: "We would have made for them, on (على) their houses, roofs". And you say to a man to his face: "I made for you, for your people, the gifts", i.e. I made it for your sake for them.
And (السُّقُف): ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it "سُقُفاً". If you wish, you make its singular saqīfa, and if you wish, you make it [the plural of] suqūf, so it is a plural of a plural, as the poet said:
حتى بلت حلاقيم الحُلُق * أهوى لأدْنى فقرة على شفق
(Until the throats of the throats [ḥuluq, plural of ḥalq] were worn out, he plunged to the nearest vertebra, with apprehension.)
And like it is the reading of whoever read "كُلوُا مِن ثُمُرِه", which is a plural whose singular is thimār; and like the saying of whoever read: "فَرُهُنٌ مَقْبوضَة", whose singular is rihān and ruhūn. Mujāhid and some of the people of the Ḥijāz read ﴿سَقْفاً﴾ like the singular, lightened, because saqf has the sense of a collective.
«[Translator's note: the verse is obscure as transmitted; the gloss is tentative.]»

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزُخْرُفاً﴾.
It is gold. It came in the exegesis: "We would make them for them of silver and of zukhruf". If you drop the من from الزخرف, you put it in the accusative by the verb, making it fall on it, i.e. "and zukhruf", We would make that for them of it. Others said: "and We would make for them, besides that, gold and wealth (غنى, shortened)", and it is the more likely of the two views to be correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
He means: whoever turns away from it; and whoever read it: "ومن يَعْشَ عن" means: whoever is blind to it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
He means the devil, and it is in [170/b] the sense of a plural, though it was uttered as a singular. He says: the devils turn them away from the path, and they think that they are rightly guided.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
So one says: (جاءنا) for one of the two, while the human and his companion came to Us. ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan read it جاءانا, in the dual; and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī, read (جاءنا) in the singular, and that is a case where one of two suffices for both. Like it is the reading of whoever read ﴿كَلاَّ لَيُنْبَذَانِّ﴾: he says: he and his wealth will be thrown; and (ولَيُنبّذَنَّ), and the meaning is the same.
«[Translator's note: «فيقتل» at the start of this paragraph is evidently a corruption (perhaps of «فيقال», "so one says"); translated accordingly.]»
His saying: ﴿يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
He means: what lies between the winter sunrise and the summer sunrise. It is also said that He meant the east and the west, and said "the two easts"; and this is the more likely of the two views to be correct, because the Arabs may combine two nouns under the name of the better known of them. So one says: "The two Zahdams have come to you", while only one of them is Zahdam. The poet said:
أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكمُ * لنا قمراها والنجوم الطوالع
(We have taken the horizons of the sky against you: ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
He means: the sun and the moon.
And another said:
قسموا البلاد فما بها لمقيلهم * تضغيث مفتصل يباع فصيله فقرى العراق مسير يوم واحد * فالبصرتان فواسط تكميله
(They divided the lands … the towns of Iraq are a single day's journey, then the two Baṣras, then Wāsiṭ completes it.)
He means: Baṣra and Kūfa.
«[Translator's note: the first half of this poetry is obscure as transmitted and is left unglossed.]»
He said: and a man of Ṭayyiʾ recited to me:
فبصرة الأزد منا، والعراق لنا * والموصلان ومنا مصر فالحرم
(The Baṣra of the Azd is ours, and Iraq is ours, and the two Mawṣils, and Egypt is ours, then the Sanctuary.)
He means: al-Jazīra and al-Mawṣil.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾.
He says: your sharing will not benefit you, meaning [the devil] and his companion. And أنكم is in the position of the nominative.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾.
An honour for you and for your people, meaning: the Qurʾān and the religion; and you will be asked about thanks for it.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
Someone may say: how was he commanded to ask messengers who had passed away? There are two views on it. One of them: that he ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel, for they only inform him of the Books of the messengers that they brought; so if he [asks] the Books, it is as though he asked the prophets.
And some said: you will be taken on a night journey, O Muḥammad, and meet the prophets, so ask them about that. But he, Allah bless him, did not doubt and did not ask them.
His saying: [171/a] ﴿أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾.
He said: ﴿يُعبَدون﴾ (masculine plural, as for rational beings) of the gods, and did not say تعبد; and they are called يُعْبَدون because the gods are spoken to, called upon and exalted, so they were treated in the same way as kings, princes and their like.
«[Translator's note: «ولم يقل: تعبد ولا يُعْبَدون» is awkward as transmitted; translated by the evident sense.]»

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا نُرِيِهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ إِلاَّ هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا﴾.
He means: than the sign that passed before it.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ﴾.
It is of the question that is made with أم because of its connection with speech before it; and if you wish, you refer it back to His saying: ﴿أَلَيْسَ لى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: one of the shaykhs informed me, I think it was al-Kisāʾī, that it had reached him that one of the readers read: "أَمَا أنا خير"; and the shaykh said to me: "Had I preserved the report about it, I would have read it so"; and it is good in meaning.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ﴾.
He means: why have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him? Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it "أساورة من ذهب", and so did the people of Medina; and it is reported of al-Ḥasan: "أَسْوِرة"; and all is correct.
Whoever read "أساورة" made its singular iswār, and whoever read "اسورة", its singular is siwār. And أساورة may be the plural of أسورة, as one says in the plural of أسقية: أساقى, and in the plural of أكرع: أكارع.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ﴾: He means: he incited them (istafazzahum).

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا﴾. He means: they angered Us.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, that he read it: "سُلُفا", with ḍamma and doubled vowels; and al-Qāsim [ibn Maʿn] claimed that he heard its singular as salīf. The generality still read: "سَلَفاً".
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us that al-Aʿraj read it: "فجعلناهم سُلُفا", as though its singular were sulfa of people, i.e. a portion of people, like umma.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to me from ʿĀṣim that he abandoned يَصُدون from the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and read يصِدون. (Al-Farrāʾ said:) And Abū Bakr said: ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Abū Razīn, from Abū Yaḥyā, that Ibn ʿAbbās [171/b] read: (يَصِدون), i.e. they clamour and cry out.
And in another report: Ibn ʿAbbās met the nephew of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr and said: "Your cousin is surely an Arab; so why does he make a mistake (yalḥan) in His saying: ﴿إذا قومك منه يصُدون﴾? It is only يصِدون." The Arabs say: يصِد and يصُد, like يشِد and يشُد, and ينمِ and ينُم from namīm (talebearing). يصدون منه and عنه are the same.
«[Translator's note: «أبى عبدالحمن» in the source is evidently Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī]; translated accordingly.]»

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy: "وإنه لذكر للساعة"; and it has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: "وإنه لَعَلَمٌ للساعة" and (عِلْمٌ), both; and all is correct and close in meaning.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰعِبَادِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾.
In the reading of the people of Medina it is: "ياعبادى", keeping the yāʾ; and ordinary speech and the reading of the generality drop the yāʾ.

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَكْوَابٍ﴾.
The kūb is the round-headed [vessel] that has no handle (ear). ʿAdī said:
خيرٌ لها إن خشيت حجرة * من ربِّها زيدٍ بن أيوبِ متكئا تصفق أبوابه * يَسقِى عليه العبد بالكوب
(Better for her, if she fears a year of drought, than her master Zayd ibn Ayyūb, reclining while his doors are clapped open and shut, the slave serving him drink with the kūb.)
His saying: ﴿تَشْتَهِى الأَنْفُس﴾: in the codices of the people of Medina: تشتهيهِ الأنفسُ وتلدُّ.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: in the punishment.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وهُم فيها مُبلسون", referring to Jahannam. The mublis is the despairing one, hopeless of deliverance.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمْنَاهُمْ وَلَـٰكِن كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
You make (هم) here a support (ʿimād, the separating pronoun), and so الظالمين is accusative; whoever makes it a noun puts it in the nominative; and it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ولكن كانُوا هُم الظَّالمون).

farraa:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ أَبْرَمُوۤاْ أَمْراً﴾.
He means: have they settled, in their own estimation, an affair that will save them from Our punishment? For We are settling [Our affair], punishing them.

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقِيلِهِ يٰرَبِّ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, Ḥamza and some of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh put it in the genitive, and the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan, as far as I know, put it in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the genitive says: "With Him is the knowledge of the Hour" and the knowledge of "his saying: O Lord". Whoever puts it in the accusative implies a verb of saying with it, as though He said: "and he said his saying", and complained his complaint to his Lord; and it is in one of the two readings [172/a]. Al-Farrāʾ said: I know it only in the reading of Ubayy, because I saw it in some codices of ʿAbd Allāh [as] وقيله. The accusative is also allowed from His saying: "نسمع سرهم ونجواهم", "and We hear his saying". And had someone said وقيلُه, in the nominative, it would be allowed, as you say: "and his call is this word: O Lord". Then He said: "فاصفَحْ عَنْهُمْ", connecting it to his supplication, as though it were from his saying, while it is from the command of Allah: He commanded him to pardon; He commanded him this before he was commanded to fight them.
«[Translator's note: the sentence about Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh is garbled as transmitted (a reading attributed to Ubayy is justified by ʿAbd Allāh's codices); translated literally.]»

farraa:89-89.t:
﴿وَقُلْ سَلاَمٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
سلام is nominative by an implied عليكم or the like; and had it been وقل سلاماً, it would have been correct, as He said: ﴿قالوا سَلاَماً قال سَلاَمٌ﴾.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
And His saying: ﴿يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾. It is also read "جاءانا" (the two of them came to Us). Whoever reads "جاءانا", the meaning is: "until, when the disbeliever and his devil came…"; and whoever reads "حَتّى إذا جاءَنا" (until, when he came to Us), it refers to the disbeliever alone. ﴿قالَ يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾: the meaning of "اَلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ" (the two easts) here is the distance between the east and the west; when they were made a pair, the word "east" prevailed (taghlīb), as the poet said:
لَنا قَمَراها والنُّجُومُ الطَّوالِعُ
(Ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
